amendments.review_rationale: Read universally Japanese ring through finite-type domain algebras and finiteness of normalization inside finite fraction-field extensions, retaining ordinary Japanese and integral closure as unassigned.
amendments.reason: Fix overly strong dependency: a universally Japanese base ring R is not required to be an integral domain. Only the finite-type algebra S in the quantifier is a domain.

references.disposition: The base ring R is an ambient commutative unital ring; the text imposes the integral-domain hypothesis on the finite-type R-algebra S, not on R.

references.matching_note: S is finitely generated as an R-algebra.
The target ring has the nonzero domain property.
Every finite fraction-field extension refers to the indexed field of fractions.

references.context: Commutative algebra: Japanese/N-2 ring property, finite normalization over finite fraction-field extensions
references.reason: The ordinary Japanese property should not be conflated with the stronger universally Japanese property.

references.phrase: integral closure of S in finite extensions
references.context: Commutative algebra: integral closure of integral domain S inside finite field extensions of its fraction field
references.reason: The integral-element property may supply prerequisite evidence but not the whole closure construction.
